name: tag-field
title: Tag Field
description: Typed words that pop into tags while the rest make room; a duplicate makes the existing tag jump instead.

perf.budget: Plain views with Reanimated layout transitions, which run only when a tag is added or removed. Nothing runs at rest.

measurements.notes: p99 spikes are the keyboard opening and closing.

a11y.reducedMotion: Tags appear and disappear at once and the rest move without a spring.
a11y.screenReader: A text field named by its label whose hint lists the tags; each tag has a Remove button. Changes are announced.
a11y.touchTarget: Each remove button is 44 by 44 pt; the field is at least 52 pt tall.

meta.guide:
## Usage

```tsx
import { TagField } from '@/components/kinetik/tag-field';

<TagField label="Topics" value={tags} onChange={setTags} maxTags={6} />;
```

## When to use

- Short free-form values people add several of: topics, skills, email recipients, labels.
- Lists where people should see and edit everything they have added in one place.

## When not to use

- Choosing from a known, short list. Use Filter Chips.
- A single value. Use Float Field.

## Notes

- Return or any of `separators` (a comma by default) ends a tag; pasted text with commas becomes several tags.
- A duplicate (ignoring case) makes the existing tag jump instead of adding another; `validate` can refuse a tag, which shakes the field.
- Backspace in the empty field first marks the last tag, then removes it. Additions and removals are announced to screen readers.
- Each remove button is a full 44 pt square inside the 32 pt pill.

docs: Prefer `npx kinetik-ui add tag-field`: it installs dependencies with expo install, so versions match your Expo SDK.
